classification.difficultyReason: Explain why identical numerical measurements give different areas when they represent base and height in one rhombus and diagonals in the other.

content.prompt: Explain why these two rhombuses have different areas.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus with horizontal top and bottom edges, one equality tick on each side, an internal vertical double-headed height arrow labelled 4 cm, and an external horizontal double-headed base arrow labelled 5 cm.
spec.mathematics: The given base is 5 cm and perpendicular height is 4 cm. Drawing coordinates preserve the source's illustrative proportions and are not additional measurements or a scale drawing.
spec.answerVisibility: All outlines, equality ticks, measurement arrows and labels are permanent student-visible givens. No area answer is drawn.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus with one equality tick on each side. Both complete diagonals are double-headed arrows. The ascending diagonal has a rotated 5 cm label and the descending diagonal has a rotated 4 cm label.
spec.mathematics: The complete diagonals measure 5 cm and 4 cm, not their halves. Drawing coordinates preserve the source's illustrative proportions and are not additional measurements or a scale drawing.
spec.answerVisibility: All outlines, equality ticks, complete diagonals and measurement labels are permanent student-visible givens. No area answer is drawn.

answer.short: The left measurements are base and perpendicular height, so $A=20\ \text{cm}^2$. The right measurements are diagonals, so $A=10\ \text{cm}^2$.
answer.worked:
The left rhombus gives the base and perpendicular height.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{left}}&=bh\\A_{\text{left}}&=5\times4\\A_{\text{left}}&=20\ \text{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
The right rhombus gives the two complete diagonals.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{right}}&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A_{\text{right}}&=\frac{5\times4}{2}\\A_{\text{right}}&=10\ \text{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
The measurements describe different lengths, so different area formulas apply.
